title: Anthropic shares close below IPO price as AI jitters return
summary:
Anthropic shares closed Tuesday at $81.91, down 6.5% and below the $83 IPO price for the first time, just four trading days after the Claude developer’s record-setting Nasdaq debut [reuters.com#1][bloomberg.com#1]. The stock opened at $111.50 on Nov. 19 and fell as low as $76.60 during Tuesday’s session; Reuters said the decline put nearly $200 billion in market value at risk [reuters.com#1].

Investors are reassessing AI companies’ valuations and computing infrastructure costs, with higher interest rates adding to financing concerns [reuters.com#1][apnews.com#1]. Anthropic also missed Monday’s rally in AI shares after Nvidia reinstated Jensen Huang as chief executive. On Tuesday, the Nasdaq fell 1.5% and the S&P 500 lost 0.5%, while the Dow rose 0.9% [reuters.com#1][apnews.com#1].

Separately, Business Insider and MarketWatch reported that employees at Anthropic and rival OpenAI have questioned internally whether the companies can safely release their most powerful unreleased models [businessinsider.com#1][marketwatch.com#1]. Anthropic said it recently delayed pretraining a new frontier model for more than a month to strengthen security [marketwatch.com#1].
quote: If we do see a slowdown in the data-center buildout, then that obviously can impact the speed at which Anthropic can develop and therefore future revenue and therefore its valuation
quote_author: Fiona Cincotta, senior market analyst at StoneX
talking_points: Index inclusion: MSCI is scheduled to add Anthropic to its global standard indexes after the Nov. 30 close; one analysis estimated passive-fund demand could equal 30% of the IPO shares by year-end [cnyes.com#3].

Chip tracking: A bill promoted by Senate Intelligence Committee Chairman Tom Cotton would require chipmakers to track advanced AI processors and notify the government if they suspect chips have reached prohibited users [myjoyonline.com#1].
Executive sale: A filing showed CEO Dario Amodei sold more than 3.37 million shares worth about $280 million to IPO underwriters as part of the offering, rather than on the open market [yahoo.com#3].

AI model debate: The White House supports open-weight AI models, whose components can be downloaded and adapted. These models can broaden demand for Nvidia computing beyond a few leading model developers; Anthropic and OpenAI have questioned their implications [ndtv.com#1].
Institutional allocation: About half of the institutional investors who placed orders for the IPO received no shares; those firms did not appear to be rushing to buy on the pullback [cnbc.com#2].

Options activity: Nearly 500,000 options contracts traded by noon Tuesday, carrying about $250 million in premiums; puts outnumbered calls roughly 300,000 to 200,000, while large trades suggested divided views [cnbc.com#1].

IPO supply: The Financial Times reported that underwriters exercised the full greenshoe option after one trading day, raising another $12.2 billion, while 315 million non-founder insider shares were eligible for sale from day one [ft.com#1].

perspectives.text: Wedbush Securities: Analyst Ygal Arounian rated the stock Outperform with a $120 target, arguing that frontier AI could serve the much larger knowledge-work market rather than just traditional software budgets. He estimated Anthropic’s market penetration at less than 1%.

CFRA Research: Equity analyst Janice Quek maintained a Buy rating, saying customers continued to use Anthropic’s services despite cheaper AI products, while warning that growing competition from open-weight models remained a risk.

Arisa Liu, a research fellow at Taiwan Industry Economics Services, said Huang’s personal ties to Taiwan remove a perceived risk that a successor might weaken Nvidia’s relationship with the island’s chip supply chain [scmp.com#5].

title: Analysts urge independent code safeguards for Anthropic's Claude Ship
summary:
Software analysts and engineers are urging caution over Anthropic’s Claude Ship, a beta service that reviews GitHub code changes, fixes problems and can approve routine pull requests under team-written policies. The service combines Code Review with two beta agents, PR Steward and Claude Approvals, to assess whether code is ready to merge [infoworld.com#1][theregister.com#1].

Analysts warn that AI systems that generate and review code may share blind spots, while automated approvals could leave teams unclear about who is accountable for a faulty change. Deepika Giri, IDC vice president for Asia/Pacific artificial-intelligence platforms and advisory, said teams should keep security scans and continuous-integration checks independent of the AI reviewer and assign a human owner to every merge [infoworld.com#1]. Nitish Tyagi, a senior principal analyst at Gartner, said models’ non-determinism makes them unsuitable as the sole quality gate [infoworld.com#1].

Anthropic recommends running approvals first in observe-only mode, where the agent reports decisions without blocking or approving merges. The company cited results from its Claude Code team but said Claude review was one layer in a broader process. Analysts say teams should assess deployments by tracking defects and rework as well as delivery speed [helpnetsecurity.com#1][decrypt.co#1][infoworld.com#1].
quote: AI models are inherently non-deterministic, which makes them unsuitable as the sole quality gate
quote_author: Nitish Tyagi, senior principal analyst at Gartner
talking_points: Usage costs: Claude Ship charges by token use. Costs depend on pull-request size and volume, review depth and PR Steward’s repair work; administrators can cap Code Review and PR Steward spending [helpnetsecurity.com#1][infoworld.com#1].

Access limits: The beta supports GitHub repositories for Claude Team and Enterprise customers but excludes organizations using Zero Data Retention, HIPAA configurations or customer-managed encryption keys [technology.org#1][helpnetsecurity.com#1].

Platform competition: Omdia analyst Lian Jye Su said Claude Ship may appeal to existing Claude Code customers, while IDC’s Deepika Giri noted that GitHub and GitLab benefit from tighter integration with their own development platforms [infoworld.com#1].

Pilot feedback: Carvana engineering executive Alex Devkar said the PR Steward pilot reduced time spent processing review feedback and allowed teams to tailor how it suggests and organizes changes [helpnetsecurity.com#1].

Benchmarking: IDC’s Deepika Giri recommended tracking spending per merged pull request, cycle time, change-failure rates, reversions and developer satisfaction before expanding beyond an initial repository [infoworld.com#1].

perspectives.text: Deepika Giri, IDC vice president for Asia/Pacific artificial-intelligence platforms and advisory: Giri warned that code-generating and code-reviewing models may share blind spots; she recommended limiting automated approvals to low-risk changes, retaining independent security checks and assigning a human owner to every merge [infoworld.com#1].

Nitish Tyagi, Gartner senior principal analyst: Tyagi said AI’s non-deterministic behavior means it should not serve as the only quality gate, and recommended distinct agent identities linked to the developer or team accountable for a pull request [infoworld.com#1].

Lian Jye Su, Omdia chief analyst: Su said Anthropic’s integration with Claude Code could attract enterprises already using its coding tools, but warned agents may not fully account for changing security and compliance requirements in some industries [infoworld.com#1].

Carvana engineering team: Senior Vice President of Engineering and Analytics Alex Devkar said its pilot helped teams spend less time addressing review feedback and allowed the tool to be adapted to their existing process [helpnetsecurity.com#1].

title: Anthropic lets Claude users install AI-built tools as Mac and Windows apps
summary:
Anthropic has begun rolling out “Install as app,” a beta feature that turns eligible tools created with its Claude chatbot into desktop apps for macOS and Windows. The apps have their own icons and windows, can be shared, and can use Claude connectors. Users can build them by describing a tool in a chat, without packaging code or setting up an API key [the-decoder.com#1][unite.ai#1][neowin.net#1][inside.com.tw#1].

The apps require an internet connection and an active Claude sign-in to open, and Claude requests count against the user’s plan limits [appleinsider.com#1][superpowerdaily.com#1][inside.com.tw#1]. Anthropic does not review apps before installation, and users decide whether to grant access to desktop features or local files [unite.ai#1][neowin.net#1].

The beta is rolling out across Claude plans, but it is limited to the Mac and Windows desktop clients; template-based Docs, Slides and Sheets artifacts cannot be installed [unite.ai#1][superpowerdaily.com#1]. Team administrators can control full computer access, while Enterprise owners must enable the feature. Anthropic has also cautioned that users should grant broad access only to apps from authors they trust [unite.ai#1][inside.com.tw#1].
talking_points: Permission tiers: Apps start with browser-level capabilities. Separate permissions can enable notifications, global shortcuts or floating windows, while full access lets apps run programs and read, change or delete files [neowin.net#1][unite.ai#1].

Update exposure: Claude requests permission again after an artifact update, but code loaded from an external website can change without prompting for renewed approval [superpowerdaily.com#1][iphoneincanada.ca#1].
Shared app use: People using a shared app that calls Claude sign in with their own accounts, and usage counts against their plans, not the creator’s [unite.ai#1].

Admin controls: Team plans allow installation by default but keep full computer access off until an administrator enables it; Enterprise plans have the feature disabled by default [unite.ai#1][biggo.com#1].

Organizational exclusions: HIPAA-ready and hybrid deployments cannot use the apps; full computer access is also unavailable to Claude for Teachers and K–12 organizations [unite.ai#1][superpowerdaily.com#1].

perspectives.text: Anthropic: The company says tools people rely on for work should open like other apps and notify users when something needs attention [siliconangle.com#1].

AppleInsider: The Apple-focused technology publication argues that mandatory internet access and Claude sign-in make the apps less useful than conventional desktop software, which can work offline [appleinsider.com#1].

title: Tidal to begin removing fully AI-generated music Dec. 9
summary:
Tidal says its systems flagged 43% of tracks delivered in the past 90 days as wholly AI-generated, with 94% of its AI-tagged catalog attributed to Suno, a music-generation platform [variety.com#1][digitaltrends.com#1]. The streaming service will begin removing fully AI-generated tracks on Dec. 9 and block new deliveries, while continuing to accept music made with AI assistance [techcrunch.com#1][rollingstone.com#1].

Tidal will use detection technology from Ircam Amplify, a French music-technology company, and screen submission metadata to distinguish fully generated recordings from work involving human creative input [gizmodo.com#1][mixonline.com#1]. A Tidal spokesperson told Rolling Stone that most appeals it reviewed upheld the AI classification, while acknowledging that some false positives are inevitable [rollingstone.com#1]. Pitchfork reported that Ircam Amplify advertises 99% accuracy and a 1% false-positive rate, and estimated that applying that rate to the takedown could mistakenly flag about 290,000 songs [pitchfork.com#1].

The policy is stricter than the labeling systems used by Spotify and Apple Music. Bandcamp also bars AI music under a broader rule covering work made substantially with AI [mashable.com#1][consequence.net#1]. Tidal expects to finish removing the tracks by early 2027 [variety.com#1].
quote: We are the first DSP to do so, and we encourage our peers to follow suit.
quote_author: Robert Anderson, Tidal lead at Block
talking_points: Low listening: Tidal said 96% of its AI-generated songs received zero plays in the previous 90 days [variety.com#1][techcrunch.com#1].

Demand mismatch: Apple Music executive Oliver Schusser said more than a third of monthly uploads were fully AI-generated, while such music accounted for less than 0.5% of listening [macrumors.com#1][apfeltalk.de#1].
Daily rejections: Tidal expects to reject 80,000 to 85,000 songs a day once the ban takes effect [variety.com#1][techcrunch.com#1].
Listener survey: An Ipsos survey across nine countries found 57% of respondents had fully AI-generated music in their playlists, while 74% thought they did not [techradar.com#1].

Rival policies: Spotify says it removed more than 75 million spam tracks from its catalog and 50 million from recommendations, while continuing to allow labeled AI music [variety.com#1][suspilne.media#1].
Impersonation removals: Tidal says it has already removed more than 65,000 tracks flagged for suspected artist-name impersonation [theguardian.com#1][cnet.com#1].

Rival responses: Spotify said it removed 50 million spam tracks from recommendations and deleted 75 million spam tracks from its catalog, while retaining labels and other measures rather than a blanket ban [theguardian.com#1][mashable.com#1].
Suno concentration: Tidal data cited by Digital Trends attributes 94% of its AI-badged tracks to Suno, a generative AI music platform [digitaltrends.com#1].

perspectives.text: Tidal: The company argues that the volume of unplayed AI uploads buries human artists and creates risks of impersonation and diverted royalties [theguardian.com#1].
Music-industry organizations: Eight groups say distinguishing AI-generated recordings from AI-assisted work protects listeners’ ability to know how music was made [ithome.com.tw#1].
Spotify: The company says its effort to limit AI spam is ongoing and that bad actors adapt quickly. It also expects listeners to value human artistry as AI makes music more abundant [variety.com#1].

Universal Music Group CEO Lucian Grainge: Grainge has argued that streaming services should pay less for AI-generated tracks than for human-made music, saying synthetic uploads can degrade the listening experience and shift value away from artists [hollywoodreporter.com#1].

Tidal: A company spokesperson said Tidal expects some false positives from its detection partner, Ircam Amplify, but described its review and appeal process as safeguards. The spokesperson said most appeals so far had upheld the original detection [rollingstone.com#1].

title: UK watchdog warns AI agents handling finances may need regulatory approval
summary:
Britain’s Financial Conduct Authority (FCA) warned technology and social media companies on Nov. 24 that AI agents may need regulatory authorization for activities involving payments, financial promotions or advice. The warning coincided with Meta’s UK launch of its Muse assistant. Meta says Muse can renew car insurance, pursue refunds and make online purchases, but the UK version cannot access bank balances or provide personalized financial guidance. Muse has surpassed 10 million downloads since its September US launch [reuters.com#1][wtvbam.com#1].

The FCA said regulatory obligations depend on what an agent does, not whether its operator calls itself a technology company, and urged developers to engage with regulators early [reuters.com#1][pymnts.com#1]. Firms using AI remain responsible for compliance even when they rely on outside providers. Consumers should check what protections apply and what personal information they share [insurance-edge.net#1][wtvbam.com#1]. A separate UK regulatory consultation on controls for AI systems remains open until Feb. 26, 2027 [financemagnates.com#1].
quote: We’ve engaged constructively with the appropriate regulatory authorities and will continue to do so.
talking_points: Operational controls: The FCA expects regulated firms to understand agents’ autonomy and risks and maintain controls that work in real time and under stress [regulationtomorrow.com#1][professionaladviser.com#1].
AI governance: Firms should track approved AI use cases in formal inventories and prevent or detect unapproved tools and software built with AI assistance [financemagnates.com#1].
Bank concerns: Banks have already urged the FCA to scrutinize AI chatbots giving financial advice to consumers [reuters.com#1].

perspectives.text: Meta: The company says it wants to connect Muse to UK banking services only after consulting regulators and obtaining any required licences [reuters.com#1].

title: Take-Two removes 3,007 repositories for GTA 6 PC port
summary:
Take-Two Interactive, the parent company of Rockstar Games, used a Digital Millennium Copyright Act notice to take down Project Leonida, an unofficial effort to run Grand Theft Auto VI on PC, across 3,007 GitHub repositories containing its code [pcmag.com#1][freepressjournal.in#1]. The company said the project facilitated copyright infringement because it was built to run leaked Xbox game files. It rejected the developers’ instruction for users to “bring your own files” as “intentionally misleading” [pcmag.com#1]. The project’s administrator, NotRexed, said its Discord server had also been taken down and ended development [eurogamer.net#1][tomshardware.com#1].

The takedown followed the circulation of an Xbox game build and a key executable, which accelerated attempts to recompile the game for Windows and other systems [pcmag.com#2][decrypt.co#1]. Leonida had reached the game’s setup screen, but footage showed a black screen afterward, not a playable port [estadao.com.br#1][gamespot.com#1]. Other teams are still working on unofficial versions, using AI coding tools to help reverse-engineer the leaked files [theverge.com#1][pcgamer.com#1]. Rockstar has not announced a PC release date. A report cited by several publications points to the first quarter of 2027, but that timing is unconfirmed [huffingtonpost.co.uk#1][pcgamer.com#1].
quote: Rockstar taking my server down was only part of the reason. Like I've said before, I'm a 15 year-old kid. Managing school and sports is hard enough without having middle aged men yell and complain to you on Discord. Goodbye.
talking_points: Leonida’s developers estimated it could take about a week to produce a playable build after the leaked executable appeared [gamespot.com#1][estadao.com.br#1].
Community shutdowns: Tom’s Hardware reported that Leonida’s Discord server had nearly 180,000 members and that Discord had banned its project account for two years [tomshardware.com#1].
Progress elsewhere: PortWatch VI ranked a group called CGBJ first, drawing on progress from XCL and Victory [pcmag.com#2].

perspectives.text: Cyberleek, who leaked GTA 6 files, described their release as opposition to what they called anti-consumer practices in the games industry. GameSpot reported, however, that the executable’s release had previously been tied to a cryptocurrency token target [gamespot.com#1].

title: Microsoft launches Code Red after outage, sets one-hour recovery goal
summary:
Microsoft has launched an internal “Code Red” overhaul after a Nov. 12-13 failure disrupted Exchange Online, Outlook, Teams, Copilot and other Microsoft 365 services for about 24 hours. The company aims to resolve future global incidents within one hour [reuters.com#1][arstechnica.com#1]. Microsoft attributed the outage to a Windows scalability defect introduced in July and said neither cyber activity nor AI agents caused it. The disruption affected government agencies, trading firms and airline communications across several countries [reuters.com#1][tovima.com#1].

The company’s review found that diagnostic information scattered across internal systems hampered its response: engineers exchanged more than 11,000 messages in 11 Teams chats without maintaining a single shared view of the incident [reuters.com#1][firstpost.com#1]. Microsoft plans to limit system load, separate traffic by region and speed recovery, with AI agents intended to help engineers interpret system-health data [reuters.com#1].

The company has not said when it expects to meet the one-hour target. Jason Henderson, president of Microsoft 365 Core, will hold daily meetings with the Substrate leadership team and weekly reviews. In a separate recent incident, an urgent fix took five to six days to reach users worldwide [reuters.com#1][arstechnica.com#1].
quote: Code Red means that this is the highest priority work for our team
quote_author: Jason Henderson, president of Microsoft 365 Core
talking_points: Failure history: Microsoft executive Charles Lamanna said the affected component had accumulated “roughly ten years’ worth of acceptable failures,” according to a memo by Amanda Silver [reuters.com#1].
Patch goal: Jason Henderson said Microsoft wants its most urgent security fixes safely deployed worldwide within an hour of detection [reuters.com#1][koreatimes.co.kr#1].

perspectives.text: Satya Nadella, Microsoft's chief executive, said better software testing and stronger system isolation could have prevented the disruption [tovima.com#1].

Brad Smith, Microsoft president, warned that more technology outages could occur in the coming months, saying AI has accelerated the discovery of weaknesses in computer code and that the infrastructure update will take more than weeks to complete [freepressjournal.in#1].

title: Nothing sets December 8 launch for AI recording earbuds
summary:

A companion app will manage recordings, transcripts and summaries. The earbuds are designed to work with multiple AI agents and Nothing’s own voice-control system [technode.com#1][androidcentral.com#1].

Users can place the case on a meeting table to record conversations without a separate recorder or phone app, while the earbuds capture phone calls [pcmag.com#1][techrepublic.com#1]. Nothing has not set a price or disclosed full specifications [technode.com#1][neowin.net#1][ubergizmo.com#1].

CEO Carl Pei said Nothing approached recording cautiously because of consent and privacy concerns. Reports on the preview also noted that the company had consulted law firms and created a London data-security team [neowin.net#1][deccanchronicle.com#1]. Nothing is due to provide more product details at the December 8 launch [ubergizmo.com#1][techgenyz.com#1].

talking_points: Privacy questions: At the preview, Nothing had not clarified whether recordings would trigger a notice to the other person or whether transcription would run on-device or in the cloud [pcmag.com#1][androidheadlines.com#1].
Button controls: The case has dedicated Talk and recording controls, and Nothing is considering letting users reassign the Talk button to other functions [neowin.net#1][technode.com#1].

perspectives.text: Nothing: The company says it obtained privacy certifications comparable to those of competing recording products [neowin.net#1].

title: Nvidia CEO Huang apologizes to staff as Trump floats pardon
summary:
Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang apologized to employees on Tuesday, acknowledged violating the company’s conduct rules and said he is in therapy. He returned as CEO a day earlier, 11 days after resigning over disclosures of affairs, including one with Alice Huang, a businesswoman whom U.S. intelligence suspects of having ties to Chinese intelligence. That relationship became entangled with an investigation into whether Nvidia chips were diverted to China through Singapore-based customer Megaspeed [scmp.com#2][bbc.co.uk#2].

At a company-wide meeting at Nvidia’s Santa Clara headquarters, Huang said it was “not acceptable” that he had broken rules he helped write. He denied that pressure from President Donald Trump had secured his reinstatement, saying the board had evaluated the facts. Trump has said he personally convinced directors to reinstate Huang. Attorney General Todd Blanche declined on Tuesday to confirm whether federal authorities had investigated Huang and described Nvidia as a “good corporate citizen” [scmp.com#2][theverge.com#1][bbc.co.uk#2].

Trump told the New York Post a pardon was “always an option” but likely unnecessary, and urged Huang to tell the truth when he appears before lawmakers. Huang is scheduled for closed-door House interviews on Dec. 1 and a public Senate hearing on Dec. 3 [ndtv.com#1][myrepublica.nagariknetwork.com#1]. Nvidia shares fell about 6% Tuesday after rising more than 31% Monday. The company’s internal inquiry and government inquiries remain active [scmp.com#2][scmp.com#1].
quote: I made some terrible mistakes
talking_points: Board scrutiny: Governance experts said the board’s reversal after publicly rejecting Huang’s return raises questions about its independence and enforcement of Nvidia’s conduct rules [cbsnews.com#1][kxan.com#1].

Spending outlook: Brian Levitt, chief global market strategist at Invesco, said Nvidia’s substantial cash flow could allow many AI-industry investments to continue, though investment and earnings growth were unlikely to return to their first-half pace [scmp.com#2].
China shipments: Nvidia said it halted shipments to China of U.S.-licensed Hopper chips, including the H200; analysts said Huang’s return does not change export restrictions [scmp.com#1].

Other inquiries: California’s attorney general has opened an investigation into Nvidia’s chip exports and shareholder disclosures, while a reported SEC accounting inquiry adds another line of scrutiny [myrepublica.nagariknetwork.com#1][forbes.pl#1].

Board oversight: Governance experts note that exchange rules require a majority-independent board, while one expert said long director tenures can undermine independence [japantoday.com#1][theglobeandmail.com#1].

Export proposals: Lawmakers may seek to add export-control measures to the annual defense policy bill during the lame-duck session; proposals include restrictions on advanced chips and chipmaking tools, as well as location verification [thehill.com#1].
Supplier exposure: The earlier rebound lifted Taiwan’s TSMC and South Korea’s Samsung and SK Hynix, along with other chipmakers and equipment suppliers across Asia [euronews.com#4][zawya.com#1].

Market warning: Charles Schwab strategist Joe Mazzola said one strong session does not establish a market bottom, with investors also pricing in a possible Federal Reserve rate increase [businessinsider.com#2].

perspectives.text: President Donald Trump: Trump said he had considered having the U.S. government take a stake in Nvidia, adding that it was “probably not too late” [ndtv.com#1].
Sen. Elizabeth Warren: The Massachusetts Democrat said she did not trust Nvidia’s internal investigation or Trump’s account of examining Huang, and called for congressional scrutiny [41nbc.com#1].

Kathleen Day, Johns Hopkins Carey Business School lecturer: Day argued that Nvidia’s directors owe their duty to shareholders rather than the CEO and said shareholders should demand a new board [japantoday.com#1].

Charu Chanana, chief investment strategist at Saxo Markets, said Huang’s return restores strategic continuity and reduces the immediate risk of supply-chain disruption. She said his relationships across the industry are difficult to replicate.

title: US jury convicts Huawei on 10 counts; sentencing set for 2027
summary:
A federal jury in Brooklyn found Chinese telecommunications company Huawei guilty on 10 of 12 criminal counts, including bank fraud, sanctions violations and conspiracy to steal trade secrets, while acquitting it of racketeering conspiracy and conspiracy to obstruct justice [al-monitor.com#1][pbs.org#1][france24.com#1]. The verdict followed a trial lasting more than two months over allegations that Huawei misled banks about its Iran business and obtained technology from U.S. companies [al-monitor.com#1][business-standard.com#1].

Prosecutors said Huawei concealed its Iran operations to preserve access to international banking and dollar-clearing services and pursued technology from competitors. The company argued that the government assembled isolated incidents into an unsupported corporate conspiracy. It has rejected the convictions and says it will appeal [cnbc.com#1][al-monitor.com#1].

U.S. restrictions have already limited Huawei’s access to U.S. technology and telecom markets. The company continues to operate internationally and has expanded into chips [theguardian.com#1][pbs.org#1]. U.S. District Judge Ann Donnelly is scheduled to sentence Huawei on September 14, 2027; potential penalties include fines, forfeiture and restitution [al-monitor.com#1][cnbc.com#1].
quote: Huawei didn't steal its way to success
talking_points: Prosecutors said Huawei ran an internal program offering bonuses to employees who obtained industrial secrets from competitors [france24.com#1].
Banking dispute: Huawei’s defense argued that HSBC and other banks knew about its Iran business and competed for the company’s account [cyprus-mail.com#1][al-monitor.com#1].
Defense case: Huawei lawyer Brian Heberlig pointed to $110 billion in research-and-development investment and $11.4 billion in technology licensing payments over two decades [ft.com#1].
Trial scale: Prosecutors called more than 60 witnesses during the trial, while Huawei’s defense called 15 [al-monitor.com#1][pbs.org#1].
5G restrictions: Before the verdict, Washington had urged countries not to use Huawei infrastructure for new 5G networks [france24.com#1][spiegel.de#1].

perspectives.text: U.S. prosecutors: Brooklyn U.S. Attorney Joseph Nocella described the verdict as accountability for what prosecutors called years of sanctions evasion, lies to banks and theft from U.S. technology companies [al-monitor.com#1].

Huawei: The company said the five trade-secret disputes cited by prosecutors had been resolved as civil matters over the past two decades and said no court had found it liable for willful misappropriation [dw.com#1].

Chinese government: Foreign Ministry spokesperson Guo Jiakun said Beijing opposed U.S. efforts to suppress Chinese companies and supported their defense of their rights and interests [al-monitor.com#1].

timeline.content: Huawei CFO Meng Wanzhou was detained in Canada on a U.S. warrant [aljazeera.com#1].
U.S. authorities publicly announced criminal charges against Huawei [business-standard.com#1].
Prosecutors added allegations of trade-secret theft from U.S. technology companies [japantoday.com#1].
Brooklyn jury convicted Huawei on 10 of 12 counts [al-monitor.com#1].
Judge Ann Donnelly is scheduled to sentence Huawei [al-monitor.com#1].

title: Saudi-led coalition strikes Yemen port after Houthis threaten Saudi ports
summary:
A Saudi-led coalition supporting Yemen’s internationally recognized government said Wednesday it struck operational targets at Hodeidah port and sites in Saada and Amran after Yemen’s Houthi movement threatened to attack Jeddah and other Saudi Red Sea ports if Hodeidah was hit [al-monitor.com#1][ndtv.com#1]. The exchange followed a Houthi drone strike Tuesday on a tower in Riyadh’s financial district, which Saudi authorities said injured 11 people [straitstimes.com#1][thehindu.com#1].

Witnesses identified the Riyadh building as the 80-story Public Investment Fund Tower, headquarters of Saudi Arabia’s sovereign wealth fund. The same tower was hit on Nov. 19, causing damage but no reported injuries [scmp.com#1][dawn.com#1]. The Houthis had not claimed responsibility for Tuesday’s strike at the time of the reports, while the coalition blamed them and vowed a response [rte.ie#1][straitstimes.com#1].

Hodeidah is a main entry point for food and other essential imports into Houthi-controlled northern Yemen, where millions depend on imported supplies [al-monitor.com#1]. Local officials said a separate coalition strike on buses and trucks in Lahj province killed 26 people on Tuesday; government forces blamed the Houthis [newarab.com#1][dawn.com#1].
quote: The port of Jeddah, along with all other Saudi enemy ports along the Red Sea coast, will become targets for our forces should the enemy carry out its threats to bombard the port of Hodeidah
talking_points: Port warnings: Houthi military spokesman Yahya Saree called on workers and nearby residents to evacuate, and urged shipping companies to withdraw vessels from Saudi Red Sea ports [al-monitor.com#1][ndtv.com#1].
Sanctions announced: Britain imposed an asset freeze on the Houthi group and asset freezes and travel bans on four senior figures, citing attempts to undermine stability [rte.ie#1][newarab.com#1].

perspectives.text: Saudi-led coalition: Coalition spokesman Maj. Gen. Turki al-Malki called the Riyadh strike a “cowardly terrorist attack” and said authorities were inspecting the site [gulf-times.com#1].

The PIF Tower was struck, damaging the building but causing no reported injuries [dawn.com#1][straitstimes.com#1]

title: China docks Shenzhou-24 at Tiangong with Pakistan's first astronaut
summary:
China’s Shenzhou-24 spacecraft docked with the Tiangong space station on Wednesday, carrying Pakistan Air Force pilot Muhammad Zeeshan Ali, the first foreign astronaut to join a Chinese crewed mission. The spacecraft arrived at 11:56 a.m. Beijing time, three hours and 38 minutes after launching from Jiuquan aboard a Long March-2F rocket [dawn.com#1][urdupoint.com#1].

Ali will spend about a week aboard Tiangong as a payload specialist, then return to Earth aboard Shenzhou-23 with two departing crew members. The Shenzhou-24 crew, led by Chinese astronaut Tang Hongbo and including flight engineer Wu Yi, will conduct more than 90 scientific experiments and technology tests [dawn.com#1][firstpost.com#1][cbsnews.com#1].

The flight is the first to carry a foreign astronaut on a Chinese crewed spacecraft and Pakistan’s first crewed orbital mission. Ali is due to conduct four joint China-Pakistan experiments. Tang and Wu will remain on the station for a six-month rotation, while Shenzhou-23 astronaut Zhu Yangzhu is staying for a year to study long-duration spaceflight [dawn.com#1][urdupoint.com#1][bbc.co.uk#2][koreaherald.com#1].
quote: I want to assure you that I am not flying for myself. I carry the name of Pakistan on my shoulder, the hopes of 250 million Pakistanis.
quote_author: Muhammad Zeeshan Ali, Pakistani astronaut and Pakistan Air Force pilot
talking_points: Docking method: Shenzhou-24 used an autonomous 3.5-hour rendezvous and docking mode; controllers can switch to a five-hour or longer approach if needed for safety [urdupoint.com#1].
Repair mechanism: Researchers will test whether solar heating outside the cabin can restore the mechanical properties of self-healing carbon-fiber composites after microcracks form [urdupoint.com#1].
Crew handover: The departing Shenzhou-23 crew includes Lai Ka-ying, Hong Kong’s first astronaut, and Zhang Zhiyuan [dw.com#1][dawn.com#2].
Seed samples: The quinoa study will expose 32 seed samples outside the station to assess how microgravity and cosmic radiation affect seed longevity and nutritional properties [urdupoint.com#1].
Microbe study: Proposed by Pakistan’s Space and Upper Atmosphere Research Commission (SUPARCO), the cyanobacteria test will run in the station’s life-ecology experiment cabinet [urdupoint.com#1].
Rocket safeguards: China’s Long March-2F team made 12 technical improvements for the flight, including a manual backup channel for separating the rocket from its launch tower [urdupoint.com#1].

Training demands: Mission commander Tang Hongbo said language and cultural differences complicated joint preparation; Ali trained in Beijing for seven months and learned Mandarin [military.com#1][japantimes.co.jp#1].
Mission record: The flight also makes Tang Hongbo the first astronaut to visit Tiangong three times, after earlier missions aboard Shenzhou-12 and Shenzhou-17 [beijingbulletin.com#2][space.com#1].

Pakistan’s ambitions: Pakistan has no spacecraft of its own for sending astronauts to orbit, and Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif has said he hopes a Pakistani astronaut will eventually reach the Moon [bbc.co.uk#2][samaa.tv#1].

Research projects: Pakistan’s space agency says Ali’s work includes cultivating microalgae as a potential source of food and oxygen and testing how spaceflight affects quinoa seeds [dawn.com#1][mediafax.ro#1].

perspectives.text: Pakistan Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif: Sharif called the mission a source of national pride and said it could inspire Pakistani young people and extend cooperation with China into space [clickorlando.com#1].

Chinese President Xi Jinping: Xi described China’s space station as a “boat” for peace, friendship and cooperation, and said Beijing was willing to deepen international space cooperation [clickorlando.com#1].

Blaine Curcio, founder of Orbital Gateway Consulting: Curcio said the mission brings Pakistan prestige, scientific and technical know-how, deeper cooperation with China and diplomatic goodwill [koreaherald.com#1].

title: Two men arrested after suspected break-in at Prince William’s Norfolk home
summary:
Police arrested two men on suspicion of burglary and trespass after responding to a report of suspicious activity at the Sandringham estate in Norfolk on Monday evening, Nov. 23. Norfolk Police said officers searched the area with police dogs, drones and a helicopter. The men remained in custody on Tuesday and had not been charged [timeslive.co.za#1][pbs.org#1][euronews.com#1]. British media identified the property as Anmer Hall, Prince William and Princess Catherine’s 10-bedroom country residence. Police said the property was unoccupied at the time [nytimes.com#1][abc.net.au#1][pbs.org#1].

The late Queen Elizabeth II gave Anmer Hall to the couple as a wedding present in 2011. They use it for holidays and short breaks, while their main residence is Forest Lodge on the Windsor estate [myjoyonline.com#1][theglobeandmail.com#1][euronews.com#1].

Norfolk Police said they are continuing to investigate. A Kensington Palace representative said the couple’s office would not comment on security matters [euronews.com#1][independent.co.uk#1].
quote: We never seem to have any trouble so when something out of the ordinary happens that sort of makes you prick your ears up and think, what was all that about?
talking_points: Estate access: The Sandringham estate covers about 80 square kilometres; visitors can access its parkland year-round, while the house and gardens are currently closed [abc.net.au#1][myjoyonline.com#2].
Recent incident: Earlier this year, police arrested a man accused of threatening Andrew Mountbatten-Windsor as he walked on the Sandringham estate [abc.net.au#1].
Nearby resident: Val Blackmur described Anmer Hall as secluded and out of view, saying people would be shocked by an attempted break-in there [myjoyonline.com#2].

Downing Street meeting: On the day the arrests were announced, William met Prime Minister Andy Burnham at 10 Downing Street to discuss homelessness, defence and security, among other topics [enca.com#1][perthnow.com.au#1].

title: B.C. towns issue evacuation alerts as storm tides threaten coast
summary:
Squamish declared a local state of emergency as communities across British Columbia issued evacuation alerts and closed waterfront areas Tuesday amid coastal flooding risks from king tides, storm surge and heavy rain. Squamish said the declaration would allow it to carry out flood-mitigation work. Parksville and the Tla-o-qui-aht First Nation warned shoreline residents to be ready to leave [timescolonist.com#1][cbc.ca#2][vancouversun.com#2].

Environment Canada warned that tides could run 20 to 50 centimetres above the highest astronomical tides through Thursday. Forecasts called for up to 225 millimetres of rain on parts of Vancouver Island, wind gusts up to 90 km/h in Greater Victoria and rapidly rising rivers across Vancouver Island and the South Coast [theglobeandmail.com#2][timescolonist.com#1].

The alerts cover coastal areas from Metro Vancouver and Vancouver Island to Haida Gwaii and the central and Sunshine coasts. Victoria closed sections of its Dallas Road waterfront seawall, and Ucluelet closed beaches and trails. The province increased highway patrols and warned that debris or flooding could force sudden road closures [vancouversun.com#1][cbc.ca#2][gov.bc.ca#1].
quote: Usually we'll get king tides, but not with a very big storm. So, this is the first time I've seen a king tide with a big storm.
quote_author: Geoff Heith, photographer and filmmaker from Port Hardy
talking_points: Highway preparations: Contractors are clearing debris from roadways and drainage infrastructure and are ready to respond [gov.bc.ca#1]

River conditions: The B.C. River Forecast Centre said peak flows could reach levels associated with a two- to five-year return period, with some weather scenarios indicating higher flows [timescolonist.com#1]

Parksville alert: The evacuation alert includes two RV resorts, a curling club, the community park, three resort or hotel properties and two Sutherland Crescent addresses; residents were told to prepare to leave on short notice [nanaimonewsnow.com#1]

perspectives.text: District of Squamish: The district said declaring a local state of emergency gives it the legal authority to complete flood-mitigation work under B.C.’s Emergency and Disaster Management Act [timescolonist.com#1].
Delta Mayor Melissa Granum: Granum said city staff know which homes have less protection and where to direct support during storm surges [cbc.ca#2].

Tla-o-qui-aht First Nation: The First Nation urged shoreline residents to take precautions and be ready to evacuate, but said it did not expect significant impacts at the time [theglobeandmail.com#2].

title: Canada says defence ties unchanged, targets spending of 4% of GDP by 2030
summary:
Canadian Defence Minister David McGuinty said Tuesday that military cooperation with the United States remains unchanged and that Ottawa does not answer to Washington. He was responding to Pentagon criticism of Canada’s spending and its review of a planned F-35 fighter purchase [globalnews.ca#1][sootoday.com#1][citynews.ca#1]. NATO’s spending commitment calls for 5% of GDP by 2035.

McGuinty said Canada is on a path to spend the equivalent of 4% of gross domestic product on defence by 2030. The federal budget projects combined defence and security spending of 4.1% of GDP in 2027-28, including 2.6% for core military spending. McGuinty’s office says the government has committed C$81.8 billion over five years to rebuild the armed forces [globalnews.ca#1][whittierdailynews.com#1][pbs.org#1]. The Pentagon says Ottawa lacks a credible, fully costed plan for the 5% goal and is delaying its largest increases until after the 2029 election [whittierdailynews.com#1][time.com#1].

McGuinty said Ottawa is focused on carrying out its plans, including rebuilding 33 bases and improving recruitment and retention [globalnews.ca#1]. Canada has not made a final decision on its F-35 order, which has been under review for more than a year [sootoday.com#1][ledevoir.com#1].
talking_points: Fleet readiness: The Pentagon said 41.9% of Canada’s air force fleet and 53.9% of its naval fleet were serviceable in 2025-26, while army readiness stood at 48% [whittierdailynews.com#1][euronews.com#1][pbs.org#1].
Procurement shift: Prime Minister Mark Carney said Canada should no longer send three-quarters of its defence capital spending to the United States [whittierdailynews.com#1][pbs.org#1].

NATO review: McGuinty said NATO allies agreed to review the 5% spending commitment in 2029, including the pace and balance of spending against security threats and military needs [coloradopolitics.com#1].
Military rebuild: McGuinty said efforts to fix a cadet challenge were also underway [globalnews.ca#1].
Aircraft alternatives: Canada has examined Swedish-made Gripen fighters as an alternative to its planned purchase of 88 U.S.-made F-35s [whittierdailynews.com#1][euronews.com#1].

perspectives.text: David McGuinty, Canada’s Minister of National Defence: He said he could not explain the Pentagon’s reasoning for criticizing Canada’s defence spending [sootoday.com#1].

U.S. Department of Defense: A senior department official said restrictions on some think-tank and social engagements were intended to create a unified objective in dealings with Canada and would not affect military operations [sootoday.com#1][lapresse.ca#1].

Erin O’Toole, former Conservative Party leader: O’Toole said the Pentagon’s account ignored changes made over the previous 18 months and described the F-35 issue as a source of leverage in the relationship [citynews.ca#1][ledevoir.com#2].

title: Alberta plans Sovereignty Act motion against federal hate speech law
summary:
Alberta Premier Danielle Smith said Nov. 24 her government will introduce a motion under the province’s Sovereignty Act opposing the removal of a Criminal Code defence for good-faith opinions on religious subjects under the federal Combatting Hate Act. The federal law took effect July 18. Smith says the change could deter lawful religious and political speech; Ottawa says the Charter protects religious expression and the law targets intentional promotion of hatred [cbc.ca#1][theglobeandmail.com#1][catholicregister.org#1].

The proposed motion would ask Alberta’s cabinet to consider further lawful steps, rather than directly cancel the federal law. Alberta Justice Minister Mickey Amery already has authority over whether many hate-speech charges proceed in the province. Constitutional law professor Gerard Kennedy said the motion could guide police and prosecutors but not bind them. The federal law also created offences targeting intimidation outside religious or cultural institutions and the public display of certain hate or terrorist symbols [cbc.ca#1][edmontonjournal.com#1][sootoday.com#1].
quote: The federal government, yes, has the constitutional authority to define what areas they believe should be in the Criminal Code
talking_points: Prosecution authority: Alberta said it recorded 14 cases involving hate-crime offences in 2025-26; Amery had no comparable figures for the period since the federal act took effect [edmontonjournal.com#1].

Provincial guidance: Amery directed Alberta Crown prosecutors in September to give significant weight to freedom of expression and not charge people simply for controversial or unpopular political or religious beliefs [catholicregister.org#1][cbc.ca#1].

Party politics: Alberta NDP Leader Naheed Nenshi called the move political theatre ahead of the United Conservative Party’s annual meeting in Calgary, while Smith denied it was aimed at the gathering [cbc.ca#1][sootoday.com#1].
Faith leaders: Edmonton Rabbi Ari Drelich said open disagreement should be protected, but speech that could lead to violence presents a serious problem [cbc.ca#1].

perspectives.text: Alberta Justice Minister Mickey Amery said the province is not planning a court challenge, describing the motion as Alberta “drawing a constitutional line” [theglobeandmail.com#1].

Federal Justice Minister Sean Fraser’s office said the law responds to calls for stronger protections against hate-motivated crime and gives law enforcement stronger tools to protect communities [cbc.ca#1][edmontonjournal.com#1].
Cardus president Brian Dijkema warned Alberta against attempting to override federal law and urged respect for the Constitution’s divisions of power [theglobeandmail.com#1].
Alberta NDP Leader Naheed Nenshi argued Smith should lobby Ottawa if she wants the federal law changed, rather than pursue a provincial motion [sootoday.com#1].

title: Ottawa seeks faster land seizures for Toronto-Quebec City rail line
summary:
Canada’s federal government has proposed giving Alto, the Crown corporation developing a high-speed rail line between Toronto and Quebec City, expanded powers to acquire land through expropriation without public hearings and transfer property directly to a private consortium [cbc.ca#1][theglobeandmail.com#1]. Transport Minister Steven MacKinnon said the measures would prevent land acquisition disputes from delaying the project for years and argued they do not remove due process [theglobeandmail.com#1][lethbridgeherald.com#1].

The proposals, included in a Budget 2026 motion published Nov. 20, would exempt Alto from the federal Expropriation Act and parts of several rail and environmental laws [cbc.ca#1][farmtario.com#1]. The project is expected to cost $60 billion to $90 billion; construction of its first phase, between Montreal and Ottawa, is scheduled to begin in 2029 or 2030 [theglobeandmail.com#1][lethbridgeherald.com#1]. Farmers, opposition politicians and municipal representatives have raised concerns about property rights, farmland and consultation, while Alto says it will pay fair compensation and limit the impacts [cbc.ca#1][farmtario.com#1].
quote: There is no removal of due process
talking_points: Property restrictions: The proposed rules could let the transport minister prohibit work on affected land for four years and preserve a government right of first refusal for as long as eight years [cbc.ca#1].

Crossing disputes: Where the rail corridor splits farms or roads, the proposal would send disputes to private arbitration, with each party potentially paying up to $25,000 plus its own legal costs [cbc.ca#1][theglobeandmail.com#1].
Farm impacts: Alto’s Montreal-Ottawa segment would cross about 1,700 properties, including roughly 500 agricultural properties, according to Alto’s chief executive [theglobeandmail.com#1].
Projected benefits: A study commissioned by Alto estimates the operating line could generate about $24.5 billion in annual economic benefits [cbc.ca#1].

perspectives.text: Avi Lewis, NDP leader: Lewis criticized the project’s public-private ownership model, saying smaller communities feel excluded and insufficiently consulted, and argued major projects need a transparent, democratic process [theglobeandmail.com#1].

Martin Caron, president of the Union des producteurs agricoles: Caron argued that bypassing ordinary expropriation rules could restrict challenges, and said the farmers’ organization is campaigning against the rail project [ledevoir.com#1].

Yves-François Blanchet, Bloc Québécois leader: Blanchet warned that the powers could extend to provincial government land and properties associated with Crown-owned utility Hydro-Québec, and called the proposal excessive [ledevoir.com#1].

title: B.C. premier directs cabinet to reverse Indigenous, climate and drug policies
summary:
British Columbia Premier Lorne Doerkson has directed his new cabinet to reverse key policies on Indigenous rights, climate action and substance use, while pursuing tax relief and tighter government spending. The government released the mandate letters Tuesday, after Doerkson and his cabinet were sworn in on Friday [theglobeandmail.com#1].

The government says ministers must focus on affordability, economic growth, health care, community safety and provincial pride, and submit new funding requests to the Treasury Board for an affordability review [castanet.net#1][gov.bc.ca#1]. The letters also call for an independent review of provincial finances as the government pledges to address a record $13.8-billion deficit [theglobeandmail.com#1].
quote: British Columbians voted for change, and our government is getting to work delivering it.
talking_points: Tax changes: Finance Minister Peter Milobar is directed to raise the basic personal tax exemption to $32,000 from $13,216 for the 2027 tax year [theglobeandmail.com#1].

Health guarantee: Health Minister Ryan Peterson is directed to make publicly funded treatment available through another quality provider when medically recommended wait times are exceeded [theglobeandmail.com#1].
School policy: Education Minister Lynne Block is directed to restore letter grades for Grades 4-9 and provincial exams, and repeal the optional SOGI 123 teaching resource [theglobeandmail.com#1].

perspectives.text: Government of British Columbia: The government says every minister must commit to a measurable result and delivery date for the five goals, and ministries must jointly develop commitments that span their responsibilities [gov.bc.ca#1].

National Observer columnist: The columnist warns that likely rollbacks to CleanBC, building and vehicle mandates, and industrial carbon pricing could leave B.C. emissions rising again [nationalobserver.com#1].

title: ESA revises BepiColombo maneuvers after Mercury insertion software fault
summary:
The European Space Agency (ESA) has revised BepiColombo’s remaining maneuvers after a software fault cut short the joint European-Japanese mission’s Mercury orbit-insertion burn. ESA says the revised sequence can correct the spacecraft’s trajectory without additional thruster burns, keeping the separation of its two science orbiters and the start of science operations on schedule [theregister.com#1][heise.de#1][newspaceeconomy.ca#1].

The fault involved attitude guidance and thruster control, and the spacecraft entered a protective safe mode when the burn stopped. The spacecraft reached a stable Mercury orbit; ESA and its partners continue to investigate the software problem [cbsnews.com#1][theregister.com#1][bug.hr#1].

The European Mercury Planetary Orbiter and Japan’s Mio orbiter remain joined and are scheduled to separate on Dec. 9–10, with routine science operations planned for April 2027. The European orbiter is expected to reach its final orbit in March, while Mio will investigate Mercury’s magnetosphere [cbsnews.com#1][physicsworld.com#1][newspaceeconomy.ca#1].
quote: After each burn, the Flight Dynamics team determines the achieved orbit to then design the next manoeuvre
quote_author: Frank Budnik, ESA BepiColombo Flight Dynamics Manager
talking_points: Orbit adjustment: The insertion burn achieved about 77% of its planned velocity change, leaving BepiColombo in a 75-hour orbit rather than the planned 58-hour orbit [theregister.com#1][cbsnews.com#1][heise.de#1].

Two investigations: The European Mercury Planetary Orbiter carries 11 instruments to survey the planet, while Japan’s Mio orbiter carries five instruments focused on its magnetosphere [physicsworld.com#1].

Weak-stability capture: BepiColombo entered orbit using a technique involving a slower approach than typical planetary insertions. Previously, only some missions to the Moon had used the technique [physicsworld.com#1][lavozdegalicia.es#1].
X-ray instrument: Before arrival, the MIXS X-ray instrument imaged the Crab Nebula to help scientists measure its angular resolution [physicsworld.com#1].

title: COP31 ends without political pact as countries pursue voluntary climate initiatives
summary:
The COP31 climate summit in Antalya ended on Nov. 22 without an overarching political agreement after countries split over whether the final text should address fossil fuels and increase climate finance [dialogue.earth#1][forbes.com#1]. Governments also pursued several voluntary initiatives outside the main negotiations [theconversation.com#1][dialogue.earth#1].

More than 80 countries backed a target to raise electricity’s share of global energy use to 35% by 2035, while the Utilities for Net Zero Alliance outlined plans for $156 billion in annual grid investment [dialogue.earth#1][forbes.com#1]. The pledge does not specify that the additional electricity must come from renewable or other low-carbon sources [smithsonianmag.com#1].

Delegates also agreed to continue climate-finance talks through 2028, without setting a new amount or baseline for increasing adaptation funding [update-eu.cz#1]. A regional Pacific roadmap for moving away from fossil fuels is expected by July 2027, ahead of COP32, scheduled for Addis Ababa, Ethiopia, the following year [dialogue.earth#1][update-eu.cz#1].
quote: If we fail on climate, the inequities we see today will grow almost beyond imagining: widespread crop failures, people losing access to water, rising conflict over basic resources, mass migration and growing tensions between countries
quote_author: Katharine Hayhoe, climate scientist at The Nature Conservancy
talking_points: Energy roadmaps: Twenty-seven governments had published or committed to publish plans for transitioning away from fossil fuels, while eight more announced plans during COP31 [dialogue.earth#1][forbes.com#1].
Treaty proposal: Thirty countries said they were working on a proposal for an international treaty to limit fossil-fuel production [dialogue.earth#1][smithsonianmag.com#1].
Building efficiency: A voluntary buildings initiative backed by 24 countries aims to cut energy use per square metre by 25% by 2035 [update-eu.cz#1].
Geothermal target: The Global Geothermal Ambition 2050 plan aims to increase global geothermal electricity and heat supply to 12 times its 2025 level [update-eu.cz#1].
Methane: Governments agreed to intensify efforts to cut methane emissions, including from fossil-fuel production, and establish new international partnerships [update-eu.cz#1].

perspectives.text: European Union and Ireland: Irish climate minister Darragh O’Brien said a pact omitting fossil fuels and a transition away from them was unacceptable; the EU and several other countries rejected the proposed text [dailymaverick.co.za#1][update-eu.cz#1].

Saudi Arabia: Saudi Arabia defended carbon capture as a practical climate response, a position that would allow continued reliance on oil and gas, according to the account of the closing negotiations [dailymaverick.co.za#1].

Chlöe Swarbrick, Green Party co-leader: Swarbrick said a deal that glossed over fossil fuels would have been a “sham” and urged New Zealand’s government to support including them in the text [scoop.co.nz#1].

Tasneem Essop, executive director of Climate Action Network International: Essop blamed developed countries for the failed talks, saying wealthy nations had gutted measures that could have protected people from worsening climate impacts [pbs.org#1].

technical_details: Carbon-removal scale: An early draft called for carbon-dioxide capture and removal to reach at least 551 million tonnes by 2035, then 1.4 billion to 2.8 billion tonnes annually; projects operating or in development are forecast to fall short of even the lower target [smithsonianmag.com#1].

Capture-project record: A review cited in the COP31 coverage found that 88% of carbon capture and storage projects from 1972 to 2018 failed because of technical or financial complications [smithsonianmag.com#1].
scientific_significance: Warming outlook: A Climate Action Tracker report said progress in slowing warming had essentially stalled over the previous five years; even if countries meet their stated plans, the world would reach about 2.6°C above pre-industrial levels by the century’s end [pbs.org#1].

Carbon-removal risks: Some proposed approaches could require extensive land for growing plants, raising concerns about land grabs and displacement, while ocean-based carbon storage may pose ecological risks [smithsonianmag.com#1].

suggested_qna.question: What separate funding mechanism did delegates agree to for the Adaptation Fund?
suggested_qna.answer: The UN Adaptation Fund is to receive a direct share of proceeds from international carbon-credit trading under Article 6.4 of the Paris Agreement [update-eu.cz#1].

historical_background: The 2015 Paris Agreement set the goal of keeping global warming well below 2°C while pursuing efforts to limit it to 1.5°C [theguardian.com#1]. At COP28 in 2023, countries agreed for the first time to call for a transition away from fossil fuels in energy systems [forbes.com#1][theconversation.com#1]. COP31 was the first climate summit since Copenhagen in 2009 to end without a final agreement, according to accounts of the negotiations [dialogue.earth#1][dailymaverick.co.za#1].

title: Anthropic mathematician claims AI-assisted proof of Riemann hypothesis
summary:
Levent Alpöge, a mathematician at artificial intelligence company Anthropic, said on Nov. 20 that he and the company’s Claude model had proved the Riemann hypothesis, a 167-year-old conjecture about the distribution of prime numbers. He released a formal proof written in 17 million lines of Lean code, which lets software check mathematical steps [wired.com#1][smithsonianmag.com#1].

The Lean Focused Research Organization and Mathlib, a volunteer-led mathematics project, said they had “full confidence” in the proof’s soundness and confirmed that its code compiles [wired.com#1]. The full argument has not yet been explained in a readily understandable form. The machine-checkable proof establishes a result without, by itself, showing researchers why it works or how to build on it [wired.com#1][arstechnica.com#1].

Mathematicians are working to digest the proof and extract its ideas. The result does not break RSA encryption, which depends on the difficulty of factoring large numbers, not on proving how prime numbers are distributed [scientificamerican.com#2][computerworld.com#1].
quote: I don't think this kind of proof would ever come from a human.
quote_author: Abhishek Saha, professor of mathematics at Queen Mary University of London
talking_points: Proof dissection: More than 60 people were using AI agents to translate sections of the proof, and contributors had produced explanations for over 3,000 segments. One mathematician estimated the work could take months [wired.com#1].
AI research: OpenAI released 722 AI-generated mathematics papers the month before Alpöge’s announcement. Some were later retracted after errors were found [theconversation.com#1].
Small result: Mathematicians have already extracted one smaller result from Alpöge’s proof and written it up separately [wired.com#1].

perspectives.text: Association for Human Mathematics: The group argued that the announcement prioritizes technical validity over clarity and accountability, and said no person can reasonably claim to understand the document [wired.com#1][elpais.com#1].

David Manderscheid, mathematician: Manderscheid argues that graduate mathematics programs should ask students not only to solve problems but also to explain and contextualize proofs, since AI can now complete work once assigned to doctoral students [theconversation.com#1].

Cybersecurity experts: Experts urged security teams to inventory cryptographic systems, replace obsolete 1024-bit RSA keys and continue planned migrations to post-quantum standards [computerworld.com#1].

did_you_know: The generalized Riemann hypothesis can help mathematicians determine which numbers can be written as a square plus another square plus seven times a third square [scientificamerican.com#2].

scientific_significance: Mathematical methods: AI systems can draw on tools across mathematical fields, but traditional work on proofs also produces connections, shortcuts and methods that other researchers can reuse [arstechnica.com#1].

Limits of AI-led discovery: So far, AI has tackled problems people already identified as important; there is no evidence it can independently recognize or formulate significant open questions [arstechnica.com#1].
industry_impact: Cryptography: Beyond the Riemann hypothesis, Computerworld reported that Claude Mythos found a mathematical flaw in HAWK, a proposed post-quantum signature standard, and a faster attack on weakened AES; AI agents have also reduced the cost of running existing software on graphics chips [computerworld.com#1].
historical_background: Riemann used the zeta function to explain discrepancies between Gauss’s estimates of prime counts and the actual counts; if true, the hypothesis would reveal order in that distribution [smithsonianmag.com#1]. In 2000, the Clay Mathematics Institute named it one of seven Millennium Prize Problems and offered $1 million for a solution [smithsonianmag.com#1][computerworld.com#1]. The institute’s prize program was intended to encourage new mathematical ideas, not simply the completion of a list of challenges, according to a September open letter signed by 28 Fields Medal winners [elpais.com#1].

title: England records 5,258 heat-linked deaths after record-hot summer
summary:
England recorded an estimated 5,258 deaths associated with extreme heat between May and September 2026, the highest total since the UK Health Security Agency (UKHSA) began monitoring in 2016 and nearly twice the previous record of 2,985 in 2022 [theguardian.com#1][bbc.co.uk#1]. The figures are provisional because death-registration data for the period are incomplete [theguardian.com#1]. The agency counted seven heat episodes lasting a total of 41 days, both records since monitoring began [reuters.com#1][bbc.co.uk#1][theguardian.com#1].

The deadliest stretch was June 21-28, when heat was associated with an estimated 2,401 deaths; more than 3,000 deaths were linked to episodes in May and June combined [reuters.com#1][theguardian.com#1]. Heat can trigger heatstroke and dehydration or worsen cardiovascular and respiratory conditions [reuters.com#1]. Dr Ross Thompson, UKHSA’s principal environmental health scientist, said periods of extreme heat are expected to become longer, more frequent and more intense as the climate warms [theguardian.com#1].
quote: The numbers are a stark reminder of the human impact of climate change, and that is why I have asked the NHS to now prepare for summer as seriously as we do for winter.
talking_points: European toll: Researchers estimated more than 50,000 heat-related deaths in urban areas across 30 European countries this summer, the highest total in their data since 2000 [reuters.com#1][aljazeera.com#1].
Health alert: England issued its second-ever red heat-health alert during the June heatwave [theguardian.com#1].

Other impacts: England recorded its driest July, with 7mm of rain. Drought was declared across all of Wales and more than two-thirds of England, and wildfires caused damage [theguardian.com#1][bbc.co.uk#1].

2050 projection: Emma Howard Boyd, chair of the National Heat Risk Commission, contrasted the 2026 toll with a Climate Change Committee projection of up to 10,000 heat-associated deaths annually across the UK by 2050 [theguardian.com#1].

perspectives.text: UK Health Security Agency: The agency said heat precautions should begin at the start of summer because people and public services may be less prepared for early-season heat, and urged longer-term adaptation of homes, neighbourhoods and health and care settings [theguardian.com#1].

Greenpeace UK: Climate campaigner Maja Darlington called the deaths a policy choice and urged the government to make fossil fuel companies pay for adaptation, while warning against approving Rosebank drilling, weakening electric-vehicle targets and expanding Heathrow [theguardian.com#1].
National Heat Risk Commission: Chair Emma Howard Boyd said the figures show an urgent public-health risk and argued that the necessary responses are already known [theguardian.com#1].

title: US consumer confidence jumps to 103.3, highest since January 2025
summary:
US consumer confidence rose 11.4 points in November to 103.3, its highest level since January 2025, the Conference Board said Tuesday. The increase exceeded forecasts and followed the Nov. 3 midterm elections. Confidence rose sharply among Democrats and independents after the election but edged down among Republicans. Respondents remained frustrated by high prices, while their assessments of jobs and the economy improved [reuters.com#1][bloomberg.com#1][cnbc.com#1].

Reduced post-election uncertainty and falling gasoline prices were cited as possible reasons for the rebound. The national average gasoline price was $3.61 a gallon on Nov. 24, down from $4.30 a month earlier but still above $3.07 a year earlier. October inflation was reported at 4%, up from 3.7% in September [theglobeandmail.com#1][abcnews.com#1].

Consumer spending had remained robust through two quarters despite weak sentiment, and economists say surveys have become less reliable measures of behavior [reuters.com#1][abcnews.com#1]. The Federal Reserve was expected to raise its benchmark rate by a quarter percentage point at its next meeting, about two weeks away, as it continued efforts to curb inflation [cnbc.com#1].
talking_points: Current conditions: The Conference Board’s Present Situation Index rose 13.7 points to 132.8, while its Expectations Index gained 9.9 points to 83.6 [hardwareretailing.com#1][cnyes.com#1].
Job perceptions: The share saying jobs were plentiful reached 30.8%, up from 26.2%; those saying jobs were hard to get fell to 18.4% from 21.4% [reuters.com#1].

Vacation plans: The share of respondents planning a vacation in the next six months reached 44.9%, up 2.2 percentage points from October, with domestic travel intentions rising and overseas plans falling [cnyes.com#1].

Uneven gains: Confidence increased across age groups, with the biggest rise among Gen Z respondents; consumers in higher-income households recorded the largest improvement [hardwareretailing.com#1][reuters.com#1].
Inflation expectations: Consumers’ expectations for inflation over the next 12 months fell for a second consecutive month but remained elevated at 5.7% [cnbc.com#1].

perspectives.text: Christopher Rupkey, chief economist at FWDBONDS, warned that trouble in artificial intelligence stock valuations could slow consumption through the wealth effect [reuters.com#1].
